title: US actor Tom Skerritt, star of Top Gun, Steel Magnolias and Alien, dies aged 93
excerpt: Skerritt served in the US Air Force before pursuing an illustrious acting career across film and television.
description: Skerritt served in the US Air Force before pursuing an illustrious acting career across film and television.
content:
Skerritt served in the US Air Force before pursuing an acting career

US actor Tom Skerritt, who starred in the TV series Picket Fences and the films Alien and Top Gun, has died aged 93, his family says.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Skerritt died on Wednesday of natural causes, his family said, adding: "While the world knew Tom through his remarkable acting career, we knew him for his humour, curiosity, wisdom, generosity and the love he brought into our lives."

In a six-decade career, he appeared in the film Mash, A River Runs Through It and Ted. He also co-founded TheFilmSchool in Seattle to support next-generation filmmakers and storytellers.

His family said he will be remembered "for his belief that stories can help people heal, find purpose and create change".

---

title: How Next-Gen AI Video Pipelines Are Transforming Global Live Broadcasting
excerpt: Broadcasting networks and independent digital studios are adopting automated AI video enhancement, instant multi-language audio dubbing, and edge transcoding.
description: Broadcasting networks and independent digital studios are adopting automated AI video enhancement, instant multi-language audio dubbing, and edge transcoding.
content:
The global media broadcasting industry is undergoing one of its most transformative shifts in decades. From real-time cloud video switching to synthetic speech translation and automated news curation, digital streaming hubs are breaking previous hardware boundaries.

---

### 🚀 The Rise of Edge Video Transcoding

Historically, transmitting low-latency live streams required massive multi-thousand dollar OB (Outside Broadcasting) trucks and dedicated satellite uplinks. Today, cloud edge transcoding algorithms can ingest multi-bitrate HLS and WebRTC video streams in under 500 milliseconds, distributing synchronized feeds across global content delivery networks.
